memory_update.text: Keep PWR as the reference benchmark for grid EPC and line construction, but avoid letting it crowd out smaller names in later Serenity layers.
MYRG is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the node because it has direct T&D electrical construction exposure and backlog disclosures that can be tracked.

PRIM is a mixed-exposure underfollowed candidate; retain only if future evidence shows electric power delivery is a material and growing driver rather than a minor segment within broader utilities work.

PLPC is the strongest second-order hardware hypothesis for this node; later layers should test whether transmission hardware orders lead EPC revenue and whether product criticality creates switching costs.

Need a later evidence pass on lineworker shortages, permitting delays, and procurement lead times to prove that labor/permitting constraints are actually shifting economics toward specialty contractors or hardware suppliers.

node: Grid EPC, transmission construction, and utility services
summary: Expanded the universe around the grid EPC and line-construction chokepoint using a two-lane funnel. Quanta Services remains the reference anchor, but the more Serenity-relevant discovery lane is MYR Group, Primoris, and Preformed Line Products: smaller public companies tied to transmission/distribution work, power-delivery EPC, or the hardware procured before field crews mobilize. The strongest underfollowed angle is that EPC backlog, lineworker scarcity, and permitting friction may surface first in specialty contractor backlogs and transmission hardware orders before appearing in utility capex realization.
